title: Moon base: the 354-hour night (method test: NASA's own footage and renderings)
note: Method test, Nov 23. Same script and voice. Every picture is NASA's own, from nasa.gov and images.nasa.gov (credit NASA): the 4K concept animation 'Living and Working on the Moon' (May 2026), NASA's animation shots in 'NASA Moon Base: The First Six Months' (Sep 2026), and four Moon Base renderings (May 2026). Shots made by NASA's partners (tagged with a company name in NASA's videos) are left out. Stills move by a slow camera push only (still_move.py).

shots.job: NASA rendering: astronauts at work at the Moon Base, a rover behind them, Earth over the horizon (still, slow push-in).
NASA concept animation: the camera glides over a base near the lunar south pole (moving).
NASA animation: a small lander on the surface, then a small rover working in the dark with its lamps on (moving). The goal's fact names landers and rovers.
NASA rendering: an astronaut beside a pressurised rover (still, slow push-in).
NASA rendering: tall solar masts catching the low Sun above a base in shadow (still, slow push-in).
NASA concept animation: the base beyond a ridge in black shadow (moving).
NASA animation: astronauts at the base, then the view pulls back to the whole Moon with one point of light (moving).
NASA rendering: astronauts and a rover on the plain, a lander on the rise, Earth above (still, slow push-in).

lines.say: A Moon base would face nights about three hundred and fifty-four hours long.
text: A Moon base would face nights

lines.say: Small landers have survived them by mostly shutting down.
Some ridges at the south pole get sunlight most of the time.
text: Some ridges at the south pole
get sunlight most of the time.

lines.say: Even the best go dark for days in some seasons.

lines.say: No base with people has yet run through a lunar night.
